DI9 Capture Masking Range
When Capture function is enabled and set to capture multiple points [ID330 (P5.038) > 1], it will stop receiving the DI captured signal within this range once the data is captured. The DI captured signal received within this range will not be recognized. This function can be used to avoid noise being regarded as effective signals within the non-capture range. Masking range is defined as follows:  [CAP_DATA- ID132 (P1 .020), CAP_DATA+ID132 (P1.020)].

Homing Collision Torque Limit
This torque limit setting is only for torque limit homing mode ID297 (P5.004.X=9 or 10). When the homing command is triggered, the motor runs in one direction until it reaches the collision protector. After reaching the collision protector, the servo drive outputs a larger motor current/torque to counter the external force from the collision protector. The servo drive uses the motor current/torque and the Torque limit time to determine homing.
See Referencing the Torque Limit in the user manual.

Homing Collision Torque Limit Time
Torque limit time setting in torque limit homing mode  ID297 (P5.004.X=9 or 10). See ID 177 (P1.087).
See Referencing the Torque Limit in the user manual.

Auto Protection Decel Time
The parameter setting is divided into D, C, B, A, U, Z, Y, X (hexadecimal), including:
1. Deceleration time when activating auto-protection function: OVF, SPL, SNL, PL, NL
2. Deceleration time of stop command: STP, PFQS
0…F is used for indexing the deceleration time of ID312 (P5.020)…ID327 (P5.035). For example: If X is set to A, then the deceleration time of PL is determined by ID322 (P5.030).

Range: 0…F
D: Function DI.STP  (0x46)
C: Function DI.PFQS (0x47)
B: Reserved
A: Function DO.OVF (0x12)
U: Function DO.SNL (0x13)
Z: Function DO.SPL (0x14)
Y: Function DI.NL (0x22)
X: Function DI.PL (0x23)

Homing Mode
Together, the X (homing mode), Y (Z pulse setting), and Z (limit setting) values determine how the homing function operates.
See Setting Homing Mode ID297 (P5.004) in the user manual.

X: Homing mode
0=Homing in forward direction and PL is homing origin
1=Homing in reverse direction and NL is homing origin
2=Homing in forward direction, ORG: Off→On is homing origin
3=Homing in reverse direction, ORG: On→Off is homing origin
4=Look for Z pulse in forward direction and use it as homing origin
5=Look for Z pulse in reverse direction and use it as homing origin
6=Homing in forward direction, ORG: On→Off is homing origin
7=Homing in reverse direction, ORG: Off→On is homing origin
8=Define current position as the origin
9=Look for the collision point in forward direction and use it as homing origin
A=Look for the collision point in reverse direction and use it as homing origin
Y: Z pulse setting
0=Return to Z pulse
1=Go forward to Z pulse
2=Do not look for Z pulse
Z: Limit setting
0=Show error when encounter limit
1=Reverse direction when encounter limit
W: Reserved

PR Command Trigger
For example, set this value to 2 to start executing PR#2.
When reading ID300 (P5.007), if the command is incomplete, the drive reads the current command (1 … 99). If the command is completed, the drive reads the current command +10000. If the command is completed, DO.TPOS is on, and motor position reached, the drive reads the current command +20000.
Commands triggered by DI are also applicable.

0=Start homing
1…99=Execute the specified PR procedure (same as using DI:CRTG+POSn)
100…999=Reserved
1000=Execute stop command (same as DI.STOP)

The start address of the data array to store CAPTURE data. Only writable when CAPTURE stops. See ID331 (P5.039).

DI9 CAPTURE Axis Position
Displays the axis position of CAPTURE pulse source.Only writable when CAPTURE stops. See ID331 (P5.039). If the source is the main encoder, this parameter is write-protected and the CAPTURE axis position is the feedback position of the motor (monitoring variable 00h).

DI9 CAPTURE Remained Count
When CAPTURE stops, it indicates the number of data expected to be captured (readable and writable).
When CAPTURE activates, it indicates the remaining number of data that has not been captured (read-only). Each time it captures one data, this value decreases by 1 until the value is 0, indicating that capturing is completed.

COMPARE Start Address
The start address of data array to store COMPARE data. Only writable when COMPARE stops. See ID351 (P5.059).

COMPARE Axis Position
Displays the axis position of the COMPARE pulse source. Writable only when COMPARE stops, but write-protected when ID351(P5.059).Y is 0 or 3 (the source of Compare axis is the Capture axis or the main encoder). 
When ID351(P5.059).Y is 3, the pulse resolution is determined by ID153 (P1.046), and this parameter is set to the feedback position of the motor (monitoring variable 00h). 
When the motor feedback position is redefined due to homing or Capture, it will be different from the parameter. In this case, set ID351(P5 - 059).Y to 0, and then set it to 3, to reset the parameter to the motor feedback position.

COMPARE Remained Count
When COMPARE is not in operation, the parameter indicates the number of data expected to be
compared (readable and writable). When COMPARE is in operation, the parameter indicates the remaining number of data to be compared. Each time it compares one data, the value decreases by one until the value is 0, indicating that comparing is completed (read-only).

DI9 First Capture Reset Position
If position reset function is enabled [ID331 (P5.039.X) Bit1 = 1], after the first position data is captured, the servo will reset the coordiates of the first point, which is defined by this parameter.

E-Cam Start Address
The start address of the data array to store E-Cam table data.This parameter can be set at any time, but is effective only at the moment when drive status changes from pre-engaged to engaged.

E-Cam Area Number
Indicates the E-Cam curve is divided into N areas, and the table should include N+1 data. Only writable when E-Cam stops. [See ID376 (P5 - 088.X) Bit0 = 0]. Its setting range must be smaller than or equal to ID303 (P5.010) minus ID369 (P5.081), and ID370 (P5.082) x ID372 (P5.084) must be smaller than or equal to 2147483647.

E-CAM Slave Cycle Number M
When receiving pulse number defined by P5.084 from the master axis, E-Cam will rotate the cycle number defined by this value (One cycle of E-Cam = Rotate from 0°…360°). Only writable when E-Cam stops. [See ID376 (P5 - 088.X) Bit0 = 0].

E-CAM Master Pulse Number P
When receiving the pulse number defined by this parameter from the master axis, E-Cam will rotate the cycle number defined by P5.083 (One cycle of E-Cam = Rotate from 0°…360°). This parameter can be
modified at any time. Its setting range must be ID370 (P5 - 082) x ID371 (P5 - 083) smaller than or equal to ID 372 (P5.084), and ID370 (P5.082) x ID372 (P5.084) must be smaller than or equal to 2147483647.

E-CAM Engaged Area Number
The area number of E-Cam when E-Cam engaged (Area number in E-Cam table).

E-CAM Master Axis Position
Position counter of the E-Cam Master. It increases when E-Cam operating. Only writable when E-Cam stops. [See ID376 (P5 - 088.X) Bit0 = 0].

E-CAM Lead Pulse Before Engaged
When the engaging condition of E-Cam ID376 (P5.088.Z) is met, the pulse number from the master axis must exceed the setting value of this parameter for the E-Cam to fully engage.
